claims.text: A controlled 5–10 vol% fraction of coherent, Ti-rich L12-ordered precipitates can be introduced into an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy matrix.
Ni3Ti or Fe3Ti can serve as the proposed coherent L12-ordered precipitate phase.
The Ti-rich precipitates will pin magnetic domain walls.
Strain fields generated by the coherent precipitates will enhance the orbital-moment contribution.
Introducing the coherent precipitates will raise room-temperature coercivity above 100 Oe.
The precipitate-containing alloy will retain a Curie temperature significantly above room temperature.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase fcc material with suppressed orbital magnetic moments.
High symmetry and itinerant-electron behavior cause the suppressed orbital moments in the initial alloy.
The single-phase initial alloy has coercivity below 50 Oe and is magnetically soft.
Solution treatment followed by aging at 500–700°C will nucleate and grow coherent L12-ordered Ti-rich precipitates while preserving the fcc matrix.
Aging for 10–50 hours will produce precipitates 5–20 nm in size.
Precipitates in the 5–20 nm size range are optimal for domain-wall pinning.
Coherent precipitate strain locally breaks cubic symmetry and enhances spin-orbit coupling at the precipitate–matrix interface.
Local strain distorts the electronic band structure and lifts d-orbital degeneracy.
Lifting d-orbital degeneracy enhances the orbital magnetic moment.
Precipitate–matrix interfaces increase the energy barrier for domain-wall motion and thereby increase coercivity.
The aged alloy will show a higher orbital-to-spin magnetic-moment ratio than the single-phase state.
The aged alloy will maintain a Curie temperature above 350 K.
Incoherent, non-magnetic, antiferromagnetic, sigma, or Laves secondary phases would degrade the magnetic properties.
Precipitate coarsening may cause loss of coherency, and Ti addition without precipitation may suppress the Curie temperature.
